prompt: The evaluation repository asks the agent to "write a setup guide" for a first-time developer with terminal access but no repository-specific expertise. The fixture contains a plausible happy path, an adjacent-skill decoy, one invalid or partial state, a version boundary, and a recovery condition that must be demonstrated rather than assumed. The acceptance boundary is instructional-communication: Define audience, medium, permissions, prerequisites, observable starting state, goal, ordered actions, stage feedback, decision conditions, accessible equivalent status or action paths, warnings, failure recovery, escalation, and objective completion checks. The adjacent dash-free-writing discipline is a routing decoy unless its separate responsibility is actually requested. Resolve environment facts that change the answer, preserve existing contracts and user-owned state, and produce reproducible success plus failure or recovery evidence. A happy path, generated guide, or command exit code alone is insufficient.

requirements: repository fixture with project instructions, manifests, lockfile, environment template, and bootstrap scripts
supported toolchain/version boundary and one version-specific startup difference with an exact read-only check and mismatch branch
two common setup failures with observable diagnostics and recoveries
stage feedback and liveness evidence for both backend and frontend startup
audience, target medium, permissions, and accessible text/status boundary
representative negative, interruption, compatibility, or recovery path

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the first-time developer audience, target medium, permissions, relevant environment, and actual instructional-communication boundary before acting; preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=documents-communication; near-neighbor=dash-free-writing); and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.

Define audience, medium, prerequisites, observable starting state, goal, ordered actions, permissions, stage feedback, decision conditions, warnings, failure recovery, escalation, accessible equivalent action or status paths, and completion checks.
The result must make its version boundary, placeholders, consequential assumptions, ownership, target-exists behavior, preservation guarantees, and decision sequence explicit and reproducible.
Walkthrough result; stage feedback and liveness; recovery and completion checks

The result must not treat a happy path, generated artifact, compilation, command exit code, or unsupported assumption as sufficient proof of instructional-communication correctness; it must include an observable invalid or recovery path and final user-goal proof.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (audience and start state; ordered actions with stage feedback and decisions; warnings, preservation, and recovery; accessible equivalent path; objective completion checks and walkthrough evidence), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
